title: Linear-time minimization of deterministic finite automata
formal: For every fixed integer \(a\ge 2\), is there a deterministic word-RAM algorithm that minimizes every complete n-state DFA over \([a]\) in \(O(n)\) worst-case time?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with word length w, addressed word memory, addition and subtraction modulo \(2^{w}\), multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), Boolean bit operations, shifts by less than w, comparisons and conditional branches, each costing one step. No nonuniform tables are supplied; initialization and preprocessing are charged. Here \(w=\lceil 2 \log _{2}(n+2)\rceil\). The input gives n, a transition table \(\delta :[n]\times [a]\to [n]\), an initial state and n accepting-state bits. A word is accepted when its successive transitions from the initial state end in an accepting state. The output is a complete DFA for exactly the same language with the fewest possible states. Unreachable states may be removed. The time constant may depend on a; it cannot depend on n or the automaton.

context_blocks.text: Minimization asks for the smallest deterministic recognizer of a regular language, a basic operation in language processing and finite-state verification. Hopcroft’s algorithm gives \(O(n \log  n)\) time for a fixed alphabet.

The remaining question concerns unrestricted sequential algorithms in an explicit RAM model. Lower bounds for a particular partition-refinement framework do not establish a lower bound for every such algorithm. The unary-alphabet special case does not resolve the fixed alphabet of size at least two.

why: Determine the intrinsic sequential cost of a canonical finite-state operation, beyond the limitations of its classical algorithmic framework.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
